title: Coherent subquotients have closed support on a locally Noetherian algebraic space
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Assume $X$ is locally Noetherian. Modules and quasi-coherence are on the small etale ringed site [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Locally Noetherian means that etale scheme charts are locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]; Noetherian means locally Noetherian, quasi-compact and quasi-separated (the diagonal is quasi-compact on scheme tests). On a locally Noetherian space, coherent means quasi-coherent with coherent pullbacks on all etale scheme charts [pqf-def-coherent]. The support of a module is the set of points with nonzero geometric stalk, in the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. The structure module $\mathcal O_X$ is coherent. If $F$ is coherent and $N\subseteq F$ is a quasi-coherent submodule, then $N$ and $F/N$ are coherent and both have closed support in $|X|$. In particular every quasi-coherent ideal $I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ has coherent quotient $\mathcal O_X/I$ with closed support.

proof.text: Work on an arbitrary etale scheme chart $e:U\to X$. Its source is locally Noetherian by the stated meaning of locally Noetherian. Pullback on modules is restriction to the localized etale site [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Restriction is exact on underlying abelian sheaves by [lem-weil-pbc-site-restriction-exact]; the same holds for modules because kernels are sectionwise and cokernels are sheafified sectionwise quotients [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Restricting local free presentations shows that quasi-coherence is preserved [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Use [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] to denote the Zariski modules corresponding to $e^*F$ and $e^*N$ by $F_U,N_U$. The chartwise coherence convention makes $F_U$ coherent. The induced map $N_U\to F_U$ is a monomorphism of $\mathcal O_U$-modules, i.e. $N_U$ is a submodule of $F_U$: the inverse of [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] is restriction to Zariski opens, so for each open $V\subseteq U$ the map $N_U(V)\to F_U(V)$ is $(e^*N)(V)\to(e^*F)(V)$, which is injective because $e^*N\to e^*F$ is monic by exact restriction and kernels are computed sectionwise [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

source.place: Tag 07UD, proof; spaces-properties.tex Tag 03LW; descent.tex Tags 03DX and 06VE(1),(5).

proof.text: The structure module has the free presentation $0\to\mathcal O_X\xrightarrow{1}\mathcal O_X\to0$, hence is quasi-coherent. On every chart its restriction corresponds to $\mathcal O_U$, which is quasi-coherent of finite type (the generator is $1$). Since $U$ is locally Noetherian, [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth] makes $\mathcal O_U$ coherent. The chartwise definition in the statement therefore makes $\mathcal O_X$ coherent.

source.place: Tag 07UB, final sentence and reduction to coherent.tex Tag 01XZ.

proof.text: Apply clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-kernel-cokernel-locnoeth] on $U$ to the coherent module $F_U$ and its quasi-coherent submodule $N_U$. Both $N_U$ and $Q_U=F_U/N_U$ are coherent. The exact comparison [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-module-exact-finiteness-comparison] sends $0\to N_U\to F_U\to Q_U\to0$ to an exact sequence in all etale modules on $U$. Its cokernel is consequently the restriction of $F/N$, since restriction is exact as established in Step 1. In particular this restriction is quasi-coherent. These local presentations also give quasi-coherence of $F/N$ on $X$: on any object of $X_{\mathrm{et}}$, use its own chart restriction, choose the local presentations there, and regard the same covering and presentations on that localized site in the definition [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. As the chart was arbitrary, both $N$ and $F/N$ now have coherent Zariski pullbacks on every chart, and are coherent in the sense stated.

source.place: Tag 07UD, proof via coherent.tex Tag 01Y1; descent.tex Tag 06VE(5).

proof.text: For $M=N$ or $M=F/N$ and any etale scheme chart $e:U\to X$, the preceding step gives a coherent Zariski module $M_U$. It is quasi-coherent of finite type by [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth], so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-module-support-closed] makes its ordinary support closed in $U$. By [lem-sfb-space-etale-chart-support], this closed set is exactly $|e|^{-1}(\operatorname{Supp}_X(M))$. The final-topology definition [def-a1-space-point-topology] says a subset of $|X|$ is closed precisely when all these inverse images are closed: apply its open-set criterion to the complement. Thus both requested supports are closed.

source.place: Tag 07TZ(1), proof via Tag 07TY and morphisms.tex Tag 056J(1).

proof.text: For a quasi-coherent ideal $I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$, take $F=\mathcal O_X$ and $N=I$. Step 2 supplies coherence of $F$ and Steps 3 and 4 give the coherent quotient $\mathcal O_X/I$ and its closed support, exactly as claimed.

source.place: Specialization of Tags 07UB and 07UD, with spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 07TZ(1).
